body:
`_probe_metadata_db()` and `cwa_get_num_books_in_library()` in `cps/web.py`
both wrap their whole body in `except Exception:` and return `False` / `0`.

Those are not error values, they are *valid-looking answers*: "the database is
down" and "the library is empty". So a programming error three lines away is
reported to the operator as a service problem.

That is what made #1438 expensive. A missing import raised `NameError` on
every call, and instead of a traceback the operator got `/health` answering
503 `degraded` while listing every service as "up" — a self-contradicting
response that reads as an infrastructure fault. The library count rendered 0
at the same time. Diagnosis took roughly two hours for a one-word omission.

The imports are fixed (#1459). The swallowing is not, and it will do this to
the next caller.

Suggested shape: catch the errors that genuinely mean "database unavailable"
(`sqlite3.Error`, `OSError`) and let everything else propagate, or log the
exception at ERROR with the traceback before returning the degraded value so
the cause is at least visible in the container log. A health endpoint in
particular should distinguish "I checked and it is down" from "I could not
run the check".
title: Health probe and book count turn any exception into a plausible wrong answer
